scope: Native two-solid thermal reconstruction and audit of coupled propulsion assumptions; no rating or area-schedule retune.

ratings.referenceScope: Published manufacturer classes retained in proposal, not a complete installed-engine performance deck.
ratings.decision: Retain existing development ratings. Requalification must jointly consider rear extraction, fan allocation, roll-post allocation, fuel model and flight-control authority.

dependencies.constraint: Dry thrust multiplied by 1 - (10000/28000)*conversion; TSFC multiplied by 1 + 1.328*conversion. Isolated 28000→27000 substitution changes the residual rear force and fuel.
20000 lbf atmospheric capacity, allocated from actual native main-nozzle upward force and longitudinal moment arms; no independent fuel.
1950 lbf per-post capacity, native main-nozzle upward-force ratio 0.10833333 and roll allocation; no independent fuel.

nozzleSchedule.meaning: Legacy native display actuator schedule, not A8, A9 or measured PW-600 throat area. Geometry defines visual radius; no thrust feedback.
nozzleSchedule.inhibitAssumption: Current XML inhibits when commanded or actual conversion is greater than zero; not a measured FADEC transition threshold.

solidRegions.name: cooled downstream liner/nozzle
solidRegions.gasBath: Nozzle gas including native actual-AB heat estimate.

solidRegions.name: core-facing turbine-exit hardware
solidRegions.gasBath: Existing native EGT + 273.15 K, upstream of afterburner heat addition.
solidRegions.modelingChoice: Lower effective mass/area and weaker cooling than downstream liner are a distinct reduced hardware hypothesis. 1800 J/K = 3 kg * 600 J/(kg K). No separate petal region is supported.

limitations: All capacities, gas flow, transfer and radiation coefficients are provisional engine-profile inputs, not F135 calibration.
Visible annular lobes are spatial optical hypotheses, not native heat zones.
The core bath is the existing scheduled EGT observation, with its existing phase behavior; no direct conversion of N1/N2 to red color.
The two solids do not directly exchange heat; each sees declared baths.
Bolometric heat-loss emissivity does not specify visible spectral emissivity.
Thermal observers retain legacy thrust/fuel/spool/EGT/nozzle behavior; they do not close an engine-cycle energy balance.
